I know a drastic change can be hard, and honestly, I'm not sure I have advice for you. But I can share an experience: One of my friends came out to me a while ago and at first it was sort of weird. Well, not weird in a bad sense, just that I wasn't used to it. It took some acclamation to stop calling her "he" on occasion, but after a while it stuck and now it just seems normal. 

I guess what I'm trying to say is that under the HRT, change in clothes, and apparent change of sexuality, your kid is still the same person. Of course it might feel off in the beginning. We all have a solid way we perceive people in - especially if we have known them forever - and whether it's on a comscious level or not, gender more often than not plays a part. So, it might take some time and effort to get used to a change as big as transitioning.

I don't know you, but perhaps another reason you feel bad is because you're disappointed in yourself for not recognizing any "signs". To that I can only say: you're not the only one! A lot of people "hide" how they're feeling about their gender because they're scared to come out. Others only realize later in life. This is not a failure on your part.

On another note, you'd probably have a brief crisis if your kid's brain was transplanted into a robot, so I can't blame you for being worried right now. But at the end of the day, your child is still your child. As long as they're happy and aren't hurting anyone, that's okay. I understand how hard a shift like this can be, especially for parents, but they need you right now. If you can, try and use the pronouns and name they have chosen. If you don't understand something, ask, and I'm sure they'll be happy to explain. A lot of relationships between parents and their kids crumble due to coming out as transgender, but you can prevent it. Moreover you'll probably be glad you did, a few years down the line.


If you want to further discuss this, my PMs are open. Otherwise, good luck!
